newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds close slightly higher.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed slightly higher across the board on Tuesday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly again today as the interbank rate eased further. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.57/98.62 compared with Monday's close of S$98.52/98.57, September 2001 at S$97.38/97.43 against S$97.26/97.31 and June 2003 at S$95.38/95.43 from S$95.26/95.31.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 2-3/4 2-5/8 percent versus Monday's 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.35/1.30 percent against Monday's yield of 1.82/1.77 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.85/1.80 percent from 2.03/1.98 percent.
